step6_output.answer_core:
Slow the situation down, keep your daughter’s trust as intact as safety allows, and get professional guidance before making irreversible choices. Talk with a therapist, RAINN, or legal counsel to help you decide if—and when—to report. Avoid abruptly shutting down her phone unless a clear safety tripwire fires.

Watch for specific tripwires that should trigger immediate escalation: any request to meet in person, sexual images or sexual talk, threats or intimidation, signs this person is also contacting other minors, your daughter saying she feels pressured or afraid, or the conversation shifting to a hidden channel after you’ve set boundaries. If any of these occur, move quickly toward protective action with professional support.

If the phone goes quiet, don’t assume the contact has stopped; it may have moved elsewhere. Keep communication open with your daughter, and share enough with the co‑parent to stay aligned on safety without letting the conversation turn into a blame fight.
